newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends off, technicals eclipse Shell news.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends off, technicals eclipse Shell news.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended lower Friday after late session gains on crude output disruptions in Nigeria failed to break technical resistance, traders said.
"We rose on the Shell news but then we came right back down since we met some pretty heavy resistance," said a New York crude dealer.
June crude ended off four cents at $19.99 a barrel. Spot crude rose as high as $20.22, failing to break resistance of $20.27, June crude's high for the week.
"Locals were just trying to push it up to find where the buy stops were, but they couldn't do it," said a dealer.
Tracking crude's losses, May gasoline ended off 0.34 cent at 62.50 cents a gallon while May heating oil ended up a mere 0.01 cent at 55.90 cents a gallon.
Royal Dutch Shell Group said it had to close its Warri flow station last weekend due to renewed clashes in the oil-producing swamps between militant youths of Ijaw and Itsekiri tribes in Nigeria.

Shell's action cut 20 percent of its Forcados crude output which traders said was equivalent to about 90,000 barrels per day of production, or just less than five percent of the average output of Nigeria, an OPEC member.
But, the state oil company, the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp, said that no cargoes had to be cancelled so far, giving the news a bearish twist.

Earlier this week, Shell had to declare a force majeure on about 500,000 barrels per day of Bonny crude in Nigeria's southeastern area because of a strike which was called off after two days. Bonny exports have since resumed.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
